items.title: THIS APPLE PAPER IS F*CKING INCREDIBLE
items.summary:
THIS APPLE PAPER IS F*CKING INCREDIBLE

Apple just proved the visual agent harness thesis from my post below

Instead of burning test-time compute on blind internal reasoning, their agent harness beats Codex and Visual Sketchpad while cutting token cost by 63%:

most developers trying to build visual agents assume that scaling inference compute or test-time thinking solves real-world perception. Apple evaluated this across 22 benchmarks and proved that scaling internal thinking alone yields diminishing returns while burning thousands of dollars in model tokens

Apple researchers analyzed multimodal execution rollouts and exposed the four fatal leaks in ungrounded vision-language models:

> test-time reasoning plateau: scaling inference budget from xhigh to max effort multiplies token spending by 2.7x but improves average score by only 0.7 points because internal reasoning cannot invent missing external facts
> raw tool output opacity: unrendered RLE masks and dense tensors consume massive context without providing interpretable visual grounding for the orchestrator
> multimodal context rot: dumping intermediate multi-turn images and bounding boxes directly into the prompt blows up context limits and degrades downstream reasoning
> computational isolation: models cannot perform multi-step geometric, spatial, or numerical calculations across heterogeneous tool outputs without code execution

their architecture, OpenVLHarness, augments an MLLM orchestrator with a core capability layer and persistent multimodal memory without editing model weights:

1. Task-Level Capability Layer
wraps heterogeneous perception, search, and coding backends (SAM 3, Grounding DINO, PaddleOCR-VL, DeepSeek-OCR, Depth Anything) behind unified typed interfaces

2. Model-Facing Evidence Rendering
converts raw tool outputs into interpretable visual attachments, labeled mask overlays, normalized bounding boxes, and compact structured summaries

3. Persistent Multimodal Memory
stores images, depth maps, and web references as addressable artifact handles outside the prompt, allowing multi-turn reuse without context bloat

4. Python Coding Agent Interface
executes generated programs directly over stored memory artifacts, calculating precise spatial distances, object coordinates, and multi-step geometric proofs

the empirical results across 22 multimodal benchmarks and 8 backbones crush standard inference:

> +9.7 to +12.6 point average score increase over matched no-tool baselines across open and proprietary models
> +11.2 on Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 on Kimi K3, +11.6 on GPT-6 Luna, and +9.9 on GPT-6 Astra
> GPT-6 Luna at medium effort with OpenVLHarness beats Codex, Visual Sketchpad, and base GPT-6 at maximum effort by +7.7 to +8.5 points
> slashes model token costs to at most 37% of maximum-effort baselines, delivering 63% cost savings while setting state-of-the-art accuracy
> establishes Pareto dominance across spatial reasoning, grounding, web search, and general visual QA

you do not solve complex visual reasoning by burning endless reasoning tokens on ungrounded internal deliberation

you solve it by pairing the model with typed tool interfaces, rendered evidence, and persistent artifact memory

inspect the paper and open-source benchmark harness at https://t.co/ArpJkSdVVN ↓

items.title: THESE 10 REPOS ARE THE F*CKING SEATBELT YOUR AGENT DOESN'T HAVE
items.summary:
THESE 10 REPOS ARE THE F*CKING SEATBELT YOUR AGENT DOESN'T HAVE

GPT-6 Cyber just built 948 working exploits, and it still stepped out of scope 0.07% of the time. your coding agent was never trained for that, and it's running on your laptop with your keys right now

one of these repos puts the agent in a box with its own kernel. another one tells you the second anything reads a fake key you planted. none of it costs a cent

10 GitHub repos to lock your agents down this week:

01 containers/bubblewrap → unprivileged sandbox. mount only the project folder, leave the network off, and the agent can't see the rest of your home
https://t.co/E8mNfUBzxf
02 google/gvisor → a user-space kernel between the agent and your machine, so a breakout hits gVisor instead of your host
https://t.co/Ft4dgzjY5X

03 firecracker-microvm/firecracker → a fresh microVM per run that boots in milliseconds and is thrown away when the task is done
https://t.co/Kp5KDZJuH9
04 mitmproxy/mitmproxy → see every request your agent makes and drop anything that isn't on the task's allowlist
https://t.co/ly7S2IWKvw

05 hashicorp/vault → short-lived scoped credentials instead of the permanent keys sitting in your .env
https://t.co/rbReAI0gP5
06 thinkst/canarytokens → fake keys and files that alert you the moment something reads them
https://t.co/XZiDkJs0Y8

07 falcosecurity/falco → runtime alerts when anything touches ~/.ssh, runs sudo or opens a shell it shouldn't
https://t.co/Zt7Fwxy0PF
08 semgrep/semgrep → finds where user input reaches a shell, a query or a file path before an attacker does
https://t.co/7uZOKkLjum

09 aquasecurity/trivy → one scan for CVEs in your images and lockfiles, plus secrets you forgot were committed
https://t.co/JChFisFpdE
10 google/osv-scanner → checks every dependency against the OSV database, so you know which holes are real before the weekend
https://t.co/zlHhQJg8Xe

do the math before you trust the 0.07%. 50 agent runs a day is roughly one out-of-scope run a month at the best rate anyone has published. at the last generation's 5.51% it's almost three a day
so make that moment boring. no open internet, no real keys on the agent's machine, a canary it should never read, and a log of every command

the repos are free. the expensive part is finding out from someone else's security team a month later
I ran the audit on a normal cloud dev box and got 3 out of 6 doors closed on the first try. run yours before you trust it

the article below has the 5 doors, the scope prompt and the audit script ↓

items.title: my digital footprint is f*cked
items.summary:
my digital footprint is f*cked

i got early access to GPT-6 Cyber ​​and connected it to Grok Bot.

then i gave it my phone number, old usernames, email addresses, and one instruction:

“find every version of me that’s still out there.”

i expected abandoned accounts.

it found an address i moved out of years ago. a profile under a username i’d forgotten. my number attached to a company i no longer work for.

then Grok started connecting the records.

different websites. different names. the same person.

me.

Grok handled the search.
Cyber ​​investigated the weak points.
Grok used the openings to reach the databases and remove the matching records.

i was watching the terminal on my phone when the first profile disappeared.

refreshed the page.

gone.

another record. another lookup. another result that no longer focused on me.

the part that got me wasn’t the code flying across the screen.

it was searching my own number afterward and getting nothing useful back.

i’d spent years blocking individual spam callers while the same information kept getting passed around.

now the phone was quiet.

no “quick question.”
no recruiter asking about a job from three years ago.
no stranger who somehow already knew my name.

i kept checking whether my phone was on silent.

it wasn't.

for once, searching for me didn’t hand someone a map of my life.

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: What is Muse Ember? Meet Meta’s new low-cost AI model | Mashable
items.summary:
As the company continues to bet that AI assistants will take on more everyday tasks, developers will need an affordable way to handle all the little steps behind the scenes. A flight search, for example, can mean sorting through dozens of fares, each with its own rules. If Meta wants people to hand off that kind of chore every day, it has to make checking the carry-on policy cheap on its end, too.

Topics Artificial Intelligence Meta

Mashable Image

Olivia Tauber [...] Meta Muse logo displayed on a phone screen is seen in this illustration photo taken in Krakow, Poland on October 25, 2026. 

Credit: Jakub Porzycki/Getty Images

Booking a vacation sounds like one thing to hand off to an AI assistant, right up until it has to check the calendar, open a dozen tabs, and figure out whether the cheapest flight is still the cheapest once a carry-on is involved. Every one of those steps takes work, and when an AI agent is doing it, the cost can add up. [...] Meta has a new model built for that part of the job.

On Nov. 9, Meta's Superintelligence Labs introduced Muse Ember"), which the company calls its smallest and most cost-efficient AI model yet. It's designed for the steps an agent might repeat dozens of times in a single assignment, like pulling details out of a document, calling another tool, or running a test after changing a line of code.

items.summary:
Cán bộ hướng dẫn công dân thao tác trên hệ thống dịch vụ công

Không chỉ hỗ trợ người dân hoàn thành thủ tục, cán bộ, chiến sĩ còn cố gắng sử dụng những cách giải thích đơn giản, dễ hiểu để người dân có thể tự thực hiện trong những lần tiếp theo. Đối với những người gặp khó khăn khi sử dụng công nghệ, cán bộ sẵn sàng hướng dẫn nhiều lần, giải đáp từng thắc mắc với thái độ tận tình, trách nhiệm. [...] Đối với những người thường xuyên sử dụng công nghệ, việc tạo tài khoản dịch vụ công, quét mã QR hoặc tải tài liệu đính kèm có thể thực hiện nhanh chóng. Tuy nhiên, với người cao tuổi và những người ít có điều kiện tiếp xúc với thiết bị điện tử, các thao tác này đôi khi gặp nhiều khó khăn.

Nhận thức được điều đó, cán bộ, chiến sĩ Công an xã Thuận An luôn chú trọng hướng dẫn cụ thể, kiên nhẫn giải thích từng bước để người dân hiểu và thực hiện đúng các thao tác cần thiết. [...] Những hoạt động hỗ trợ tuy giản dị nhưng mang ý nghĩa thiết thực, góp phần giúp người dân thuận lợi hơn trong giải quyết thủ tục hành chính, tiết kiệm thời gian, chi phí đi lại và từng bước nâng cao kỹ năng sử dụng dịch vụ công trực tuyến. Qua đó, Công an xã Thuận An tiếp tục đưa công nghệ đến gần hơn với người dân, nhất là những người còn gặp khó khăn trong tiếp cận công nghệ, để mọi người đều có cơ hội thụ hưởng những tiện ích của chuyển đổi số.

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: What is Muse Ember? Meet Meta’s new low-cost AI model | Mashable
items.summary:
As the company continues to bet that AI assistants will take on more everyday tasks, developers will need an affordable way to handle all the little steps behind the scenes. A flight search, for example, can mean sorting through dozens of fares, each with its own rules. If Meta wants people to hand off that kind of chore every day, it has to make checking the carry-on policy cheap on its end, too.

Topics Artificial Intelligence Meta

Mashable Image

Olivia Tauber [...] Meta Muse logo displayed on a phone screen is seen in this illustration photo taken in Krakow, Poland on October 25, 2026. 

Credit: Jakub Porzycki/Getty Images

Booking a vacation sounds like one thing to hand off to an AI assistant, right up until it has to check the calendar, open a dozen tabs, and figure out whether the cheapest flight is still the cheapest once a carry-on is involved. Every one of those steps takes work, and when an AI agent is doing it, the cost can add up. [...] Meta has a new model built for that part of the job.

On Nov. 9, Meta's Superintelligence Labs introduced Muse Ember"), which the company calls its smallest and most cost-efficient AI model yet. It's designed for the steps an agent might repeat dozens of times in a single assignment, like pulling details out of a document, calling another tool, or running a test after changing a line of code.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. [...] Create opportunities for local workers and businesses.We’ll publish the jobs we expect to create, work with unions and training providers to help residents prepare for them, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.

items.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation, source says | Reuters
items.summary:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round ​that values the company ​at $1.25 trillion, a source familiar with ⁠the matter said on Friday.

The $11 ​billion raised so far represents ​only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, while ​the company's valuation has ​come down from the $1.5 trillion level it ‌had ⁠initially sought, two investors said. items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
